text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Leaders of the ruling party in Kenya's central province endorse the removal of a former district chairman from branch leadership.
- Opposition parliamentarians say they will protest to the International Monetary Fund and World Bank because a visiting team refused to meet them.
- An Ethiopian delegation visits Kenya for talks over the killing of 80 people in cross-border raids by bandits.
- A plainclothes policeman draws a pistol and threatens to shoot an opposition activist at a Sunday service.
- British businessman John Ward, whose daughter Julie was murdered more than eight years ago, is to see the attorney -general to press for release of an independent police report.
- Opposition Democratic Party Chairman Mwai Kibaki declares his support for Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
- An official of opposition FORD-Asili party discloses a plot to disrupt the forthcoming general elections.
- Sixty family members are relocated by the government in the Rift Valley to ease tension between neighbouring Pokot and Marakwet communities.
- Kenyan leaders caution diplomats against meddling in the country's internal affairs.
- Kenya's call for suspension of the Burundi sanctions is a sign of a crack behind the region's united approach to Burundi.
- Tanzania imposes strict rules barring top-level managers previously involved in the running of collapsed financial institutions elsewhere in the world from employment.
- A public relations contract to restructure Uganda's Ministry of Information runs into trouble. ($1=54 Kenya Shillings)
